comparison: Perfect agreement on the paired data design methodology (C10, C53, C180, C185). Both recognize this as an important methodological innovation that controls for systematic biases. Reviewer 1 explicitly praises the sequential stimulus protocol as increasing sensitivity and allowing detection of subtle effects.

Strong agreement on adaptational changes as a major finding (C9, C36, C69-C75, C181-C183). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers recognize this as one of two major discoveries. Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'About a third of the retinal ganglion cells display cell-type specific adaptation' and validates the feature-selectivity and type-specificity.

Strong agreement on main findings (C5-C6, C37-C40). Both confirm NO's selective effects on G32 subtypes. Editor states 'compelling evidence' and reviewers explicitly validate cell-type specificity and selective modulation. OpenEval R6, R10, R13, R15 provide detailed support for components of these main findings that peer review R1 also addresses (C79-C87, C105-C113, C132-C138, C144-C147).

Agreement on lack of spatial RF effects (C119-C124, C139). Both OpenEval and Reviewer 1 confirm NO modulates temporal but not spatial properties. This negative result is treated as an important characterization of NO's selective action.

Divergence on NO concentration interpretation (C167-C169). OpenEval finds the concentration physiologically relevant and well-justified. Reviewer 1 expresses uncertainty, finding it 'perhaps surprising that this relatively low NO concentration produced significant effects,' though acknowledges possible explanations without rejecting the findings.

Agreement on strychnine control experiments (C65-C67). OpenEval explicitly validates this as an appropriate positive control. Peer reviewers implicitly accept it as part of the validated experimental system, with Reviewer 1 noting the sequential protocol controls were effective.

Agreement on classification validation (C59-C61). Both confirm the approach recapitulates prior landmark studies. Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'cell-types revealed by the analysis largely recapitulate those from their earlier landmark study,' validating the reliability.

Agreement on speculative nature of functional interpretation (C7, C148-C151, C8). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is plausible but lacks direct evidence. Peer reviewers accept it as reasonable speculation without challenge, treating the study as providing 'valuable new information' with 'broad interest.'

Agreement that functional role claims (C8) are speculative. OpenEval explicitly notes lack of direct evidence about actual signaling function. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as appropriate speculation by not challenging it and recognizing the study's value.

Agreement on MEA sampling differences (C130-C131). Both accept this technical limitation as adequately explained. Reviewer 1 acknowledges complementary nature of methods without raising concerns about sampling differences.

Agreement on artificial stimuli limitation (C155-C156). OpenEval finds the acknowledgment appropriate with reasonable justification. Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'limitations of the method and data interpretation are adequately discussed in the revised manuscript.'

Agreement on value of complementary methods (C189). Both validate the Ca-imaging and MEA approach. Reviewer 1 explicitly states the methods 'provide complementary approaches' demonstrating NO's selective effects, treating this as a strength.

Agreement on G32 subtype clustering and differential NO effects (C105-C113). OpenEval validates the clustering methodology and quantitative characterization. Peer review R1 confirms these findings as part of the main results showing selective modulation of G32 subtypes.

Agreement on MEA confirmation of Ca2+ imaging results (C132-C138). Both recognize the reversibility, independent clustering confirmation, and cross-validation as major strengths. Peer reviewers validate the complementary evidence from independent methods.

Agreement on primary NO effects on G32 (C76-C87). OpenEval validates the statistical approach and feature-based characterization. Peer review R1 confirms these as part of the main findings showing NO selectively increases activity in contrast-suppressed RGC types.

Agreement on MEA findings summary (C144-C147). Both confirm convergence of evidence from two independent methods. Peer reviewers validate that MEA recordings complement Ca-imaging in demonstrating temporal but not spatial modulation.

Agreement on MEA-specific findings including faster kinetics (C139-C143). OpenEval validates the novel temporal kinetics finding and reasonable explanation for why Ca2+ imaging missed it. Peer review confirms NO modulates temporal properties as demonstrated by MEA.

Agreement on complex effects in G31 and G18 (C88-C92). OpenEval validates the interpretation that G31 effects are primarily adaptational and acknowledges weaker G18 effects. Peer review R1 accepts these findings as part of the overall pattern of selective effects.

Agreement on many RGC types being unaffected (C93-C96). Both recognize this demonstrates feature- and type-specificity. Peer review R2 confirms 'DETA-NO selectively increases activity in a subset' implying others are unaffected.

Agreement on clustering analysis methodology (C97-C104). OpenEval validates the coverage factor argument and clustering approach. Peer review R1 accepts the identification of three clusters as part of the validated main findings.

Agreement on technical considerations and bias assessment (C178-C180, C183-C184). OpenEval validates that type-specific, feature-selective changes argue against systematic bias. Peer review R3 implicitly accepts this through validation of the paired data design methodology.

OpenEval validates experimental protocol details (C4, C41-C54) including recovery times, light adaptation, sequential recording, and sample sizes. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found, though these methodological details underpin the validated sequential protocol approach.

OpenEval validates acknowledgment of photopic conditions constraint (C161-C164) and speculation about light-level dependent functions. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found for this specific limitation.
OpenEval validates discussion of SbC cell context (C172-C177) and correspondence to prior literature. No corresponding explicit peer review evaluation found for this specific contextual discussion.
